title: Hypotheses and measurable outcomes
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of hypotheses and measurable outcomes
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: An observation or analysis chosen after seeing evidence

blocks.text: After seeing faster responses, the team changes its primary claim from support improvement to speed improvement.
Report the change as exploratory/post-result revision. Preserve the original support hypothesis; do not present speed as the prespecified primary outcome.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Before running12 cases, you expect B support to exceed A. Write primary metric and one falsifying result.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Primary metric is supported cases/12 under the fixed rubric. Equal or lower B support contradicts the strict-improvement expectation in this sample.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A hypothesis can fail honestly; changing it after results does not erase the original test.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
